# Data and models

**Field.** GLORYS12V1 reanalysis on its native $1/12^\circ$ grid. OHC is the $0$–$2000$ m depth
integral of potential temperature against constant $c_p\rho$ (`code/ohc.py`), evaluated daily over
2010–2019. Cells enter the analysis only where $\mathrm{deptho} > 2000$ m *and* the integral is
defined at every level.

**Mean field.** OHC is split as $\mathrm{OHC} = \hat m + \tilde Z$ into a smooth climatological mean
field $\hat m$, fitted once across $1995$–$2019$, and the residual anomaly field $\tilde Z$. $\hat m$ is a per-cell OLS on a quadratic trend
plus annual and semiannual harmonics, fit against the GLORYS *monthly* record with each basis
function averaged over its month to match the monthly-mean response, then evaluated pointwise per
day. @sec-meanfield gives the estimator and summarizes what it leaves.

**Advection.** OceanParcels, park depth $1000$ m, advected by GLORYS daily $(u,v)$ over
$11$–$66^\circ$ N, $87$–$12^\circ$ W -- the full 2010-2019 footprint of every float that profiles an
analysis box in 2015-2019, so simulated floats are not deleted for leaving the velocity domain (an
earlier $15$–$50^\circ$ N, $70$–$30^\circ$ W domain lost most such floats at its western edge; see
@sec-retention). Floats advect continuously at park depth and record a position every $10$ days;
there is no ascent, descent or surface drift, so a cycle is a position sample, not a simulated dive.
Floats are deleted on leaving the velocity domain and retired at a lifespan drawn from the real Argo
record for this region (median $\approx 1500$ d).

**Estimation.** $\hat Z_k$ is the unweighted mean of $\tilde Z_k$ at the profile positions for year $k$, and $\bar Z_k$ is the exact $\mathbb{P}$-weighted domain mean
of the same field for year $k$.

# The analysis domain

Two analysis boxes sit inside the downloaded GLORYS region, both spanning $60^\circ$–$40^\circ$ W:
**Box B** ($35$–$45^\circ$ N) straddles the North Atlantic Current and the Gulf Stream extension,
and **Box A** ($22$–$34^\circ$ N) has milder currents and OHC variability. Temperature was downloaded for the analysis boxes and a small buffer; velocity was
downloaded over a larger region to advect floats, which are lost if they exit the velocity domain.

# Mean field {#sec-meanfield}

The sampling-bias question concerns the *residual anomaly* OHC field, not the total.  We therefore decompose

$$\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) \;=\; \hat m(c,t) \;+\; \tilde Z(c,t),$$

with $\hat m$ a mean field fitted per cell once across all years and $\tilde Z_k$ the year-$k$ residual the designs sample. 

**Regression.** For each analysis cell $c$, OHC is modelled as
$\mathrm{OHC}(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \beta_c + \varepsilon(c,t)$ on the trend-plus-harmonics basis
$\phi(t) = \bigl(1,\,t,\,t^2,\,\sin 2\pi t,\,\cos 2\pi t,\,\sin 4\pi t,\,\cos 4\pi t\bigr)^\top$
($t$ in decimal years): a quadratic trend and the annual and semiannual cycles. The coefficients are
fit by least squares to the $1995$–$2019$ GLORYS *monthly* mean record.

A GLORYS monthly file holds the month *mean*
OHC over $I_m = [t_0^m, t_1^m)$ but is time-stamped at its start $t_0^m$. So we regress
on the **window-averaged basis** $\bar\phi(I_m) = |I_m|^{-1}\!\int_{I_m}\phi(t)\,dt$, so the OHC monthly response and seasonal basis are monthly averages. The design matrix is $\bar X = \bigl[\bar\phi(I_m)^\top\bigr]_m$ and the per-cell fit is 
$\hat\beta_c = \bar X^{+} Y_c$. **Prediction is then pointwise:** the fitted field is evaluated at each instant on the daily grid, $\hat m(c,t) = \phi(t)^\top \hat\beta_c$, and subtracted from daily OHC to give $\tilde Z_k = \mathrm{OHC}_k - \hat m$ on the same mask.

# Estimand, truth, and estimator

Let $\mathbb{P}$ be the normalized area $\times$ time probability measure over the depth masked analysis domain.
The target is the residual field's
domain mean,

$$\bar Z_k \;=\; \int_{\mathcal{X}} \tilde Z_k \, d\mathbb{P},$$

for each analysis year $k$, where $\tilde Z_k$ is the year-$k$ OHC 0–2000 m field with the fitted mean
field removed. A design is a finite point set $\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{n} \subset \mathcal{X}$ — the year-$k$
in-box profiles of one deployment realization $d$; its estimator and bias are

$$\hat Z^{(d)}_k \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \tilde Z_k\!\left(x_i^{(d)}\right),
\qquad
B^{(d)}_k \;=\; \hat Z^{(d)}_k - \bar Z_k .$$

$\tilde Z_k$ is a simple function on the native $1/12^\circ \times$ daily grid, so evaluating it at
$x_i$ is the cell-day lookup of the *containing* cell.

```{python}
#| echo: false

HTML(fmt(rp.truth_table()))
```


$\bar Z_k$ would be zero if the 1995–2019 mean-field fit were exact on the analysis years; the table above
carries the small per-year misfit (largest $\bar Z_{2011} = -1.63$ GJ/m$^2$ in Box B), which is
mean-field misfit, not sampling, and cancels from $B$ by construction (@sec-meanfield). The dispersion
$\sigma_k = \mathrm{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k)$ is $6.3$–$7.6$ GJ/m$^2$ in Box B and $1.7$–$2.4$ in
Box A.

# Deployment

One continuous advection per realization generates the sampling. For realization $d$, $N$ floats are
seeded uniformly over normalized spacetime across the velocity record of 2010-2019.
Each realization therefore yields $B^{(d)}_k$ for
every analysis year at once, flow and field the same calendar year. 

**How a float is advected.** Each float is carried by GLORYS12V1 daily horizontal velocity $(u,v)$ at
a fixed park depth of $1000$ m and held there for its whole life — there is *no dive cycle*. The two
archived velocity levels bracketing $1000$ m ($902$ and $1062$ m) are linearly interpolated to the
park depth (as OceanParcels does natively), and the float is stepped forward at a $1$-hour time step. Its position is written every $10$ days, and that recorded
park-depth position is taken as the profile — the point where a real float would begin its ascent — so
a cycle is a position sample, not a simulated dive. A float is deleted when it leaves the velocity
domain and retired at a lifespan drawn from the real Argo record (median $\approx 1500$ d).

::: {.callout-note}
This version reflects the **expanded velocity domain** ($11$–$66^\circ$ N, $87$–$12^\circ$ W). The
pilot below is a **preliminary $16$-realization re-run** on that domain (the full $100$-rep run is
pending); its confidence intervals are correspondingly wider. The argo-actual comparison arm
(@sec-argo-cmp) is on the new domain; the resampled argo-bootstrap ensemble has been removed pending
its re-run.
:::

The pilot is **$16$ independent realizations** (preliminary; target $100$). Each seeds **$1{,}000$
floats** uniformly over normalized space–time on the ($\mathrm{deptho}\ge 1000$ m) region spanning
both boxes plus an $8^\circ$ margin, across $2010\text{-}01\text{-}01$ to $2019\text{-}12\text{-}26$,
and advects them once at $1000$ m park depth ($10$-day profiling cycle, lifespans drawn from the real
Argo record). Years $2010$–$2014$ are the equilibration lead; bias is calculated on **$2015$–$2019$**.



::: {.panel-tabset}

## A single deployment cluster {#sec-cluster}

Six floats were deployed within a $\sim\!14$-hour window on $27$–$28$ September $2015$ in a tight
cluster in the NW corner of Box B ($43.4$–$44.3^\circ$ N, $-55.8$ to $-57.8^\circ$ W), on the Grand
Banks / Gulf Stream–Labrador confluence. They are a clean natural experiment in deployment geometry:
a common release point and time, whose per-float sampling bias we can then follow profile by profile.

For the simple-mean estimator the year-$k$ bias is an *exact* sum of per-profile contributions.
Writing $n_k$ for the number of in-box profiles the array reports in year $k$,

$$
B_k \;=\; \hat Z_k - \bar Z_k
\;=\; \frac{1}{n_k}\sum_{i=1}^{n_k}\bigl(\tilde Z_k(x_i) - \bar Z_k\bigr)
\;=\; \sum_{i=1}^{n_k} c_i,
\qquad
c_i \;=\; \frac{1}{n_k}\,\underbrace{\bigl(\tilde Z_k(x_i) - \bar Z_k\bigr)}_{\delta_i},
$$

the centering being free because $\tfrac{1}{n_k}\sum_i \bar Z_k = \bar Z_k$. Every profile carries the
*same* weight $1/n_k$ whatever float it came from — that equal weighting is what makes the estimator
the simple (unweighted) mean, and it ties the normalization to the year, not the float. Grouping the
contributions by float gives each float's share of the year's bias,

$$
C_{f,k} \;=\; \sum_{i\,\in\, f,\,k} c_i \;=\; \frac{n_{f,k}}{n_k}\bigl(\bar Z_{f,k} - \bar Z_k\bigr),
\qquad \sum_f C_{f,k} = B_k,
$$

its profile share $n_{f,k}/n_k$ times its mean alignment $\bar Z_{f,k} - \bar Z_k$ (with
$\bar Z_{f,k}$ the mean of $\tilde Z_k$ over that float's year-$k$ in-box profiles).

The charts below plot the single-profile bias $\delta_i = \tilde Z_k(x_i) - \bar Z_k$ — one profile's
alignment with the field — along each float's life (in-box profiles only, where the residual field is
defined), with the cluster mean over-plotted. This is the contribution $c_i$ up to the $1/n_k$ weight;
we show $\delta_i$ rather than $c_i$ so the curves stay comparable across years (the year's $n_k$ only
rescales them). The two tabs evaluate $\delta_i$ at the *real* Argo positions and at the *GLORYS
park-advection* sim-twin positions of the same floats, so their divergence is the same
real-vs-reanalysis gap the trajectory maps show.

::: {.panel-tabset}

# The sampling weight field

The bias  $B^{(d)}_k = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, w^{(d)} - p\rangle$, the inner product of
the residual field with the excess of the empirical sampling weight over the uniform weight p.
One realization's sampling is the normalized empirical measure

$$w^{(d)} \;=\; \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} \delta_{x_i}$$

on the spacetime domain $\mathcal{X} = \mathcal{A} \times \mathcal{T}$. Averaging it over realizations gives
$\mathbb{E}[w]$, the normalized occupancy (intensity) measure of the advective array, with
$\mathbb{E}[B_k] = \langle \tilde Z_k,\, \mathbb{E}[w] - p\rangle$.

We define the spatial marginal sampling weight as

$$w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c \;=\; \sum_{\tau\in\mathcal{T}} w_{c,\tau} \;=\; \frac{\#\{\,i : x_i \in c\,\}}{n},$$

the fraction of a realization's profiles that fall in cell $c$, summed over all days. The maps below
show $\mathbb{E}[w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c]$ — the expected such fraction, i.e. the array's normalized spatial
intensity — over the years $2015$–$2019$ on the native $1/12^\circ$ grid, against the uniform
area marginal $p^{\mathrm{sp}}_c = A_c / \sum_{c'} A_{c'}$, as the ratio
$q_c = \mathbb{E}[w^{\mathrm{sp}}_c] / p^{\mathrm{sp}}_c$ ($=1$ under area-fair sampling).

## Bias as a covariance

Let $q = w/p$ be the sampling frequency of each cell-day relative to its
uniform share — the over/under-sampling factor mapped in @fig-wspace and distributed in @fig-whist,
equal to $1$ under uniform sampling and with $\int q\,\mathrm{d}\mathbb{P} = 1$. The bias is the inner
product of the field with the sampling excess,

$$B_k \;=\; \langle \tilde Z_k,\, q - 1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}}
       \;=\; \langle \tilde Z_k - \bar Z_k,\, q - 1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}},$$

the second equality because $\langle 1, q-1\rangle_{\mathbb{P}} = 0$ — a spatially uniform field is
sampled without bias. Cauchy–Schwarz for this inner product gives the cap

$$|B_k| \;\le\; \lVert \tilde Z_k - \bar Z_k\rVert_{\mathbb{P}}\,\lVert q - 1\rVert_{\mathbb{P}}
         \;=\; \sigma_k \, \operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q),$$

with $\sigma_k = \operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(\tilde Z_k)$ (the residual-field table) and $\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q)$
the spread of the over/under-sampling factor (@fig-whist), attained only when $q-1$ is proportional to
the field anomaly. **Zero bias does not require uniform sampling** — it requires only that $q - 1$ be
orthogonal to $\tilde Z_k$ in $L^2(\mathbb{P})$; a strongly non-uniform array
($\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q) \gg 0$) can still be unbiased for this functional.

# Real-deployment comparison: deployment vs. drift {#sec-argo-cmp}

The real Argo array is markedly more biased than the uniform-seeded simulation (@fig-bias). To
separate how much of that gap is the *geometry* of where and when Argo is deployed from how much is
real float motion diverging from the simplified advection, the **argo-actual** arm seeds the *same*
GLORYS park advection from the real Argo deployment record instead of uniformly in space–time: each
cleaned float's first profile inside the box-plus-$8^\circ$ margin over $2010$–$2019$ ($365$
deployments, with their real positions, dates, and lifespans), advected verbatim (one realization,
the direct fidelity check). On the expanded velocity domain almost none of these floats are lost to
domain exit (@sec-retention), so the arm now scores far more of each real deployment's in-box life
than it could before.

```{python}
#| echo: false

HTML(fmt(rp.argo_comparison_table(est, argo_actual, argo), 3))
```


```{python}
#| label: fig-argo-cmp
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Deployment-law comparison per box: uniform ensemble (grey) intervals, the single actual-deployment realization (orange diamond), and real Argo (green X), all on the expanded velocity domain."

rp.plot_argo_comparison(est, argo_actual, argo)
plt.show()
```

Seeding from the real deployments moves the Box B bias from essentially zero (uniform) to negative:
the argo-actual mean over $2015$–$2019$ is $\approx -0.48$ GJ/m$^2$, against the real array's
$\approx -0.73$ — so the verbatim park advection of the real deployments reproduces **roughly two
thirds of the real Box B bias**. Where and when Argo is actually put in the water, carried by the
flow, lands profiles preferentially over cold anomalies, something uniform-in-space–time seeding does
not reproduce. The remaining $\sim\!0.25$ GJ/m$^2$ is the residual the park-only advection cannot
capture — real trajectories diverging from GLORYS (ascent/surface drift/descent, real currents
$\neq$ reanalysis). Year by year the sign matches the real array in $2015$–$2018$; only $2019$ flips
positive ($+0.64$), a single noisy realization. Box A stays small under both deployment laws.
(A resampled real-deployment *bootstrap* ensemble, which puts a Monte-Carlo spread around this single
realization, is being re-run on the expanded domain and will be restored here.)

## Is the residual gap the missing dive cycle?

The park-only sim omits the dive cycle — the ascent, the $\sim\!1$-day surface drift, and the descent
— so one reading of the residual $\sim\!0.3$ GJ/m$^2$ is that a profile recorded at the $1000$ m park
position sits systematically away from where a real float actually surfaces. To test this we advect
each real deployment verbatim at park depth, keeping the full drift path, and compare the GLORYS-park
track to the *same* real float's profile positions over time.

```{python}
#| label: load-divergence
#| include: false

div = rp.trajectory_divergence()
```

```{python}
#| echo: false

HTML(fmt(mm.trajectory_divergence_summary(div), 1))
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-divergence
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Great-circle separation between each real Argo float and its GLORYS-park sim twin vs days since deployment (median and IQR over 365 floats), against the level two independent floats reach (dashed)."

rp.plot_trajectory_divergence(div)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-twins
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Two long-lived real Argo floats and their GLORYS-park sim twins from a shared deployment (star; real end a filled circle, sim end an open square). Each float is a matched colour pair -- real the darker solid line, sim twin the lighter dashed line: a Box A float in blue/cyan (~8 yr, subtropical gyre) and a Box B float in purple/pink (~6 yr, NAC / Gulf Stream)."

rp.plot_trajectory_twins()
plt.show()
```

The sim loses the real float fast: median separation is already $\sim\!53$ km at one $10$-day cycle,
$\sim\!135$ km at a month and $\sim\!290$ km at three, climbing through $\sim\!590$ km at a year
(@fig-divergence). The field's mesoscale correlation length is $\sim\!50$–$100$ km, so the GLORYS-park
position exceeds it *within a single cycle* and is several correlation lengths off well inside the
analysis year — it samples effectively independent locations at the seasonal scale that sets the bias.
Individual twins make this concrete (@fig-twins): a subtropical-gyre float and its twin part slowly,
while a NAC / Gulf-Stream float and its twin split early and end up in different parts of the basin.
A dive cycle would add only the $\sim\!1$-day surface excursion per cycle (tens of km, largely
non-persistent), far too small to produce or repair a divergence that grows at $\sim\!5$ km/day. **So
the drift residual is reanalysis and advection error — real $1000$ m currents and unresolved eddies,
not the missing surfacing — and adding a dive cycle to the advection would not close it.** (The
$\pm 6$-day matching tolerance inflates the $10$-day point; the month-plus separations dwarf it, and
the separation also bundles the surface-vs-park offset, which only reinforces the conclusion.)

# Conclusions

From this $100$-realization pilot:

**The advective sampling bias is small but not zero.** In both boxes $\mathbb{E}[B_k]$ stays within
$\sim\!0.02\,\sigma_k$ (the bias tables) — a few hundredths of a GJ/m$^2$ against a field varying by $6$–$8$
(Box B) and $2$ (Box A) GJ/m$^2$. It is not identically zero: several years are resolved at $2$–$4$
Monte-Carlo standard errors, so the array is weakly preferential in effect, at a magnitude that is a
small fraction of the field's own variability.

**Strong non-uniform sampling, nearly orthogonal to the field.** The array samples space genuinely
non-uniformly (on-mask up to $\sim\!3.6\times$ over-sampling, $\operatorname{sd}_{\mathbb{P}}(q)\approx0.4$;
@fig-whist), yet the bias is only $\sim\!1$–$5\%$ of the Cauchy–Schwarz ceiling that non-uniformity
permits, i.e. a weight–field correlation $|\rho_k|\approx0.02$. Preferential sampling does not imply
preferential bias for this functional — the estimand-level bias is the covariance
$\operatorname{Cov}_{\mathbb{P}}(q,\tilde Z_k)$, and the array sits near its null space, not a property of sampling
non-uniformity per se.

**Both regimes are comparably biased once standardized.** Box B has larger raw bias and spread, but on
the $\sigma_k$ scale the energetic western-boundary region is not disproportionately biased relative to
the quiescent gyre.
